findings.title: New-conversation acceptance still erases a newer unsaved draft during automatic navigation
findings.description: The revision-bearing accepted event correctly preserves B while its original new:<project> owner is mounted. However, Workspace.send always navigates to the newly created thread after conversation/start succeeds if navigation.current is unchanged. Typing B changes the draft revision, not navigation.current. The automatic key switch then reads an empty draft for the new thread and replaces the only in-page B copy and its warning. Thus the same R23 input-loss guarantee remains unfulfilled for the new-conversation entry point.
findings.trigger: Persist A under new:p, start conversation/start, keep response pending, type B while draft setItem throws QuotaExceededError, then return accepted with created-thread ID.

validation.method: Real current useDraft, Api, drafts and operation modules transformed in memory with Node's TypeScript transformer. The exact Workspace.send source expression is extracted unchanged. Unrelated UI dependencies are inert substitutes; navigate reproduces its navigation counter and setThreadId behavior. Synthetic fetch, isolated jsdom, fresh fake IndexedDB. This is a focused source-level integration probe, not a full Workspace browser test.

findings.repairBoundary: Make post-acceptance new-conversation handoff conditional on preserving the current draft owner, or implement a safe explicit handoff of newer memory state. Do not weaken new-key isolation or erase all current fields. Add a focused actual new-conversation send/acceptance regression with memory-only B and its warning.
